findings.title: ValidationError interpolation leaks the raw API response body into logs and the web UI log viewer
findings.problem: The old form logged only `exc.error_count()`. The new form interpolates the whole `pydantic.ValidationError`, and pydantic's `__str__` embeds an `input_value=` rendering of the offending payload for every error. Confirmed empirically against this repo's own SystemStatus model. The redacting sink in triggarr/logging.py only does exact-substring replacement of known secret values, so any other sensitive or unexpected field the *arr instance returns in a malformed response passes through verbatim, into `buffer_sink`/`log_buffer`, and is rendered to the web UI log viewer (routes.py:389 and :1199). A multi-error validation failure also emits a multi-line message into a buffer whose LogEntry model assumes a single line.
findings.fix_hint: keep the count-only form, or log `exc.errors(include_url=False, include_input=False)` so field locations are logged without echoing the response payload
findings.why_it_matters: The project's stated convention is that API keys and sensitive data never reach logs, responses, or HTML; the redaction sink is an exact-match backstop for known secrets only, so echoing an arbitrary upstream payload into a UI-visible buffer defeats it for anything unknown.

findings.title: Diff is a byte-for-byte revert of security fix d47b4c2 — raw httpx exception logged instead of status code
findings.problem: This diff is a byte-for-byte revert of commit d47b4c2 'fix(security): prevent potential key leakage in validate_connection log messages' (2026-04-09); both hunks restore the pre-fix form verbatim. The codebase has an established type-based sanitization helper for exactly this, `_sanitize_exc()` in triggarr/search/engine.py:30 ('Avoids storing raw str(exc) which may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink'), used at 25+ call sites across engine.py, scheduler.py, and routes.py; scheduler.py:400-403 documents the convention explicitly. The two reverted lines are now the only httpx/pydantic exception log sites in the changed file that pass the raw exception. `httpx.HTTPStatusError.__str__` embeds `request.url`; the redacting sink only replaces configured secret values.

findings.title: ValidationError logged raw instead of via the established _sanitize_exc / error_count form
findings.problem: Second instance of the same deviation, on the pydantic branch. `_sanitize_exc` handles `pydantic.ValidationError` with the identical formulation the diff deletes: engine.py:43 returns `f'validation error ({exc.error_count()} issues)'`. The removed `count=exc.error_count()` was that established form inlined; `exc=exc` replaces it with the full multi-error ValidationError repr, which echoes back the offending input values from the *arr API response.
findings.fix_hint: Use `exc=_sanitize_exc(exc)` here, matching triggarr/web/routes.py:612-613 and the engine.py call sites.
findings.why_it_matters: Listed as a retained architectural lesson in .planning/RETROSPECTIVE.md (type-based exception sanitization to avoid information leakage), not an authorized exception.

findings.title: _sanitize_exc lives in search/engine.py — importing it into clients/base.py would close an import cycle
findings.problem: Structural obstacle to the obvious fix: `_sanitize_exc` lives in triggarr/search/engine.py, which imports triggarr/clients/{radarr,sonarr,lidarr}.py, each of which imports triggarr/clients/base.py. Importing `_sanitize_exc` from engine.py into base.py would close a cycle base.py -> engine.py -> radarr.py -> base.py. Underneath is a pre-existing layering inversion: a secret-redaction primitive consumed by the client, web, and scheduler layers is owned by the search-engine module and reached via a leading-underscore private name across package boundaries (routes.py:53, scheduler.py:47).

findings.fix_hint: Move `_sanitize_exc` to a leaf module (triggarr/logging.py is the natural home), re-export from engine.py for compatibility, then import it from there in base.py, routes.py, and scheduler.py. For THIS diff, a plain revert avoids the question entirely.
findings.why_it_matters: Whoever applies the `_sanitize_exc` fix in base.py will hit the cycle mid-fix unless the helper is relocated first.

findings.title: ValidationError interpolation leaks *arr API response body fragments into the web-exposed log buffer
findings.problem: The old message logged only `exc.error_count()`. The new `{exc}` interpolates the full `str(pydantic.ValidationError)`, which renders an `input_value=...` fragment echoing the offending API response payload (verified by constructing the real failure against SystemStatus). This message reaches both the stderr redacting sink and `buffer_sink`, which stores it in the module-level `log_buffer` (maxlen=200) that routes.py:389 and :1199 render into the web UI log viewer. Redaction only replaces values in the `collect_secrets()` list; anything else the misbehaving upstream returns in a /system/status body (reverse-proxy error pages, auth-portal HTML, session identifiers) is echoed verbatim to any authenticated log-viewer user. Bounded because pydantic truncates input_value and SystemStatus is the only model validated on this path.
findings.current_code:
except pydantic.ValidationError as exc:
            logger.warning(
                "{app}: Unexpected API response format: {exc}",
                app=self._app_name,
                exc=exc,
            )
            return False
findings.fix_hint: Log a bounded projection instead of the whole exception, e.g. `exc.error_count()` plus the field locations (`[e['loc'] for e in exc.errors()]`), which gives the diagnostic value without echoing `input_value`.
findings.why_it_matters: The log buffer is a web-rendered surface, and the redaction sink is an allowlist of known secrets, not a general scrubber. Any upstream-controlled bytes interpolated here are published to the UI unfiltered.

findings.title: HTTPStatusError interpolation puts the full instance URL (including userinfo credentials) into the web log viewer
findings.problem: The old message logged `exc.response.status_code`. `str(httpx.HTTPStatusError)` embeds the complete request URL and httpx does NOT mask userinfo (verified: `https://user:pass@radarr.local:7878/...?apikey=SECRET123` stringifies verbatim). The config-layer guards do not close this: `reject_apikey_in_url` (models/config.py:66-90) rejects only query keys starting with `apikey` and explicitly allows `?token=`; `validate_arr_url_config` (web/validation.py:112-172) never inspects `parsed.username`/`parsed.password`. So `https://user:pass@radarr.local` and `?token=<secret>` are accepted config, neither is in the `collect_secrets()` redaction list, and both now render verbatim in the UI log viewer on any non-401 HTTP error. The retry path at base.py:66-76 already solved this by projecting to `f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"`.
findings.current_code:
logger.warning(
                    "{app}: Unexpected HTTP error: {exc}",
                    app=self._app_name,
                    exc=exc,

findings.fix_hint: Follow the existing convention at base.py:71-75: log `f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"` (or status plus `exc.response.reason_phrase`) rather than the exception object.
findings.why_it_matters: Instance URLs are user-supplied config that the validators permit to carry credentials in userinfo or non-apikey query params; those bytes are outside the redaction allowlist and land on a rendered web page.

findings.title: Validation error formatting can bypass secret redaction
findings.problem: Logging the full ValidationError includes response input values when version is missing or invalid. If a misconfigured upstream returns credential-bearing JSON, Pydantic can truncate a credential before the logging sinks apply exact-string redaction. A local reproduction with a missing version and an apiKey field logged the key prefix unchanged after redaction. This exposes response data in stderr and the web log buffer; the previous error-count message avoided this.
findings.fix_hint: Keep the error count, or log only validation locations and error types without input values or context. Add a regression test using a credential-bearing invalid response and verify that neither full credentials nor truncated fragments reach either logging sink.
findings.why_it_matters: This exposes response data in stderr and the web log buffer; the previous error-count message avoided this.
